page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled, delivering a dedicated CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 64 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and includes 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES cryptography, and SHA-NI instructions. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing placing the instance in the top 25% of evaluated systems. Multi-core performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth is consistent, recording 1013.33 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 93.7 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The instance demonstrates strong text generation speeds for small language models, achieving 277.2 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model, while larger workloads like 7B parameter model inference and database operations perform at average levels.

From a resource density perspective, the n2d-standard-16 offers a balanced cost-to-performance profile for standard workloads that do not require local SSD storage or GPU acceleration. The lack of local storage means all storage operations rely on network-attached persistent disks, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy applications. This instance is configured for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, software compilation, medium-scale database operations, and general application hosting.
